title: Reset-arm regression guard pin is not unique — also matches the pre-existing consent-changed opt-out arm
evidence:
Makefile:274: 	           'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' \
Dockerfile:133:     && grep -q -F 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' server/priv/static/index.html \
The pinned substring occurs TWICE in the analytics snippet (grep -o | wc -l = 2):
  (1) NEW reset arm: ..."rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset();...
  (2) PRE-EXISTING consent-changed opt-out arm: ...opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;}});...
detail: The pinned substring already existed in the consent-changed opt-out arm, so reverting only the new reset-arm clear would still satisfy both build guards. The new logout cookie-clear — a session-hygiene fix — is not actually regression-pinned.
recommended_fix: Extend the pin to the reset-arm-only suffix, e.g. '...SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset()' (the consent arm ends '...rtPhId=null;}}'). Apply in BOTH the Makefile (l.274) and Dockerfile (l.133) guards.

title: OAuth sign-in now sends landlord email to PostHog server-side, consent-independent (mirrors email/password path)
evidence:
auth_handler.gleam:1128:           posthog_client.identify_with_set_once(
auth_handler.gleam:1129:             posthog,
auth_handler.gleam:1130:             row.id,
auth_handler.gleam:1131:             [#("email", json.string(row.email))],
No consent gate precedes the call; compare process_signup at auth_handler.gleam:258-261 which fires the same consent-independent identify_with_set_once on the email/password path.
detail: Email PII is transmitted to a third-party processor (PostHog) on every Google sign-in with no analytics-consent check server-side, matching the in-production email/password posture. Disclosed in code comments; recorded for the privacy/consent record.
recommended_fix: No code change if the posture is intentional — email/password is the precedent. Confirm the documented privacy posture covers server-side PII transmission to PostHog across both auth paths.
